comparisons.peer_topic: Capital and RWA Changes at Year-End 2024
comparisons.peer_summary: At December 31, 2024, CET1 capital increased to $201.1 billion, Tier 1 capital rose $135 million, and Total capital under Standardized approach increased $4.0 billion, while RWA grew $44.5 billion to $1,696 billion driven by client and lending activity.
comparisons.comparison: Both Goldman Sachs (GS) and Bank of America (BAC) disclose specific year-end 2024 capital metrics and the composition of capital changes. GS reports a CET1 ratio of 15.0% and advanced returns of $11.80 billion, while BAC reports a CET1 capital amount of $201.1 billion (a $6.2 billion increase) and notes that RWA grew to $1,696 billion. Both filings highlight the interplay between capital generation, distributions, and regulatory ratios, though GS focuses on the resulting ratio percentage while BAC provides the absolute dollar change in capital.

sentences.text: As of December 2024, our CET1 capital ratio was 15.0% under the Standardized Capital Rules and 15.3% under the Advanced Capital Rules.
At December 31, 2024, CET1 capital was $201.1 billion, an increase of $6.2 billion from December 31, 2023, primarily due to earnings, partially offset by capital distributions.

comparisons.peer_topic: Shareholder Returns and Capital Repurchase Program
comparisons.peer_summary: Citi returned $6.7 billion to shareholders in 2024 via dividends and repurchases, and authorized a new $20 billion multiyear repurchase program in January 2025 with $1.5 billion planned for Q1 2025, subject to regulatory capital uncertainty.
comparisons.comparison: Both GS and Citi (C) disclose the total amount of capital returned to common shareholders in 2024. GS returned $11.80 billion via repurchases and dividends, whereas Citi returned $6.7 billion through the same mechanisms. Both companies frame these returns within the context of their capital management strategies, although Citi explicitly links its future repurchase capacity to regulatory capital uncertainty, a constraint not explicitly mentioned in GS's summary of the 2024 return.

sentences.text: During 2024, we returned a total of $11.80 billion of capital to common shareholders, including $8.00 billion of common share repurchases and $3.80 billion of common stock dividends.

• Citi returned $6.7 billion to common shareholders in the form of dividends ($4.2 billion) and share repurchases ($2.5 billion) in 2024. As previously disclosed, on January 13, 2025, Citigroup's Board of Directors authorized a new, multiyear $20 billion common stock repurchase program, with planned repurchases of $1.5 billion during the first quarter of 2025, subject to market conditions and other factors. After the first quarter of 2025, Citi will continue to assess the level of common share repurchases on a quarter-by-quarter basis given uncertainty regarding regulatory capital requirements, among other factors.

comparisons.peer_summary: Citigroup's CET1 Capital ratio increased to 13.6% as of December 31, 2024, from 13.4% in 2023, driven by net income and a decrease in risk-weighted assets, partially offset by dividends, share repurchases, and AOCI movements.
comparisons.comparison: Both GS and Citi report their CET1 capital ratios as of December 31, 2024, and note the drivers of their capital positions. GS reports a CET1 ratio of 15.0% (Standardized) and 15.3% (Advanced). Citi reports a CET1 ratio of 13.6%, noting that the increase from 13.4% was driven by net income and decreased RWA, partially offset by dividends and repurchases. GS's disclosure similarly references Note 20 for capital ratio details, while Citi explicitly attributes the ratio movement to specific balance sheet and income factors.

sentences.text: As of December 2024, our CET1 capital ratio was 15.0% under the Standardized Capital Rules and 15.3% under the Advanced Capital Rules.
Citigroup's CET1 Capital ratio was 13.6% as of December 31, 2024, compared to 13.4% as of December 31, 2023, based on the Basel III Standardized Approach for determining risk weighted assets (RWA).

comparisons.peer_summary: As of the end of 2024, the Firm reported CET1 capital of $275.5 billion, with Standardized and Advanced CET1 ratios of 15.7% and 15.8%, respectively, and a Supplementary Leverage Ratio (SLR) of 6.1%.
comparisons.comparison: Both GS and JPMorgan (JPM) disclose their CET1 capital ratios and amounts for the end of 2024 using both Standardized and Advanced approaches. GS reported a CET1 ratio of 15.0% (Standardized) and 15.3% (Advanced). JPM reported a CET1 capital of $275.5 billion with ratios of 15.7% (Standardized) and 15.8% (Advanced). Both firms maintain strong capital positions above regulatory minimums, with JPM providing the absolute capital dollar amount while GS provides the ratio percentages directly in the overview.
